title: Noise sensitivity of linear threshold functions
statement:
There exists a real constant $C\ge0$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every $\{-1,1\}$-valued function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ that is the threshold of a real polynomial of degree at most one, and every $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, its noise sensitivity satisfies
\[
\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)\le C\sqrt{\delta}.
\]
Here the polynomial threshold assigns $1$ to nonnegative values and $-1$ to negative values, and noise sensitivity is defined from the noise stability at parameter $1-2\delta$ by $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)=(1-\operatorname{Stab}_{1-2\delta}(f))/2$.
hypotheses_covered: there exists a real constant C
f has a polynomial threshold representation of degree at most one
replaced:
There exists a universal real constant $C\geq0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every linear threshold function $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(c+\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i(-1)^{x_i})$ on $\{0,1\}^{n}$ with real coefficients and every $0<\delta\leq1/2$,
\[
\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\leq C\sqrt\delta.
\]
Here $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, and $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)=\Pr[f(X)\neq f(Y)]$ with uniform $X$ and independent coordinate flips of probability $\delta$ producing $Y$.
